newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says pointless to set forex targets at G7.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says pointless to set forex targets at G7.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said in a newspaper interview on Friday that there was no sense in trying to set exchange rate targets at this weekend's G7 meeting in Berlin.

Asked whether the group would accede to Japan's wish for exchange rate goals to boost the weak yen, Waigel told Die Welt: "You can't determine exchange rates with statements. No movement can be achieved against the market with communiques."
Waigel added: "It is not possible to determine exchange rates, but you can adopt the required policy and then implement it. Every country must do its homework. That applies to Japan."
The Finance Minister repeated remarks he has made recently that he saw the recent sharp gains by the U.S. dollar against the mark as a "normalisation" of the dollar weakness of 1995.

That did not mean that the German mark would become a weak currency, Waigel said. He added that the turnaround in forex markets reflected changes in purchasing power and strong U.S. economic fundamentals.
"I really see no problems. On one hand the strong dollar will boost our exports. On the other, the strong dollar poses no inflation risks. We have inflation under control," he said.
